name: Edgeguard
goal: Keep an opponent knocked off the stage from getting back onto it
why: An opponent off the stage has to get back onto it, with only its jump and its specials, by the ledge or straight onto the stage. Each way can be covered: the ledge taken first, a hit on the way, a punish on the landing or on the way up from the ledge. Kept off the stage, it loses its stock at percents where a hit on the stage would not take it.

tutorial.what: The opponent is knocked off the stage and has one aim: to stand on it again. Take its stock first.
tutorial.expect: A try runs until the opponent loses its stock, or stands on the stage again, free to act, or Fox is lost. The ledge is not the end: from it the opponent still has to get up past you, and a hit sends it out to start again. It picks its way from where it is, stalls and waits, and takes another way when it sees what you commit to, its reaction time after you do.

marks.1: Frame 1: X or Y, Fox's back to the ledge
marks.J+1: Frame {J+1}: air dodge down and back, the first frame in the air
marks.J+2: Frame {f}: Fox slides back off the edge and catches the ledge

lessons.title: Back to the stage
text: A fighter off the stage has to stand on it again. It comes straight onto the stage or by the ledge, with its double jump, if it is left, and its specials. Most specials leave it helpless: once one has started, where it ends is decided.
An edgeguard covers where it ends: the ledge taken first, a hit on its way, a punish on its landing. From the ledge it must still get up past you.

marks.1: Frame 1: X or Y, Fox's back to the ledge
marks.J+1: Frame {J+1}: air dodge down and back, the first frame in the air
marks.J+2: Frame {f}: Fox slides back off the edge and catches the ledge

cues.words: Air dodge down and back now

lessons.title: Taking the ledge
text: Only one fighter hangs from a ledge. With Fox's back to it, X or Y and an air dodge down and back on frame {J+1} slides him off the edge: he catches the ledge facing the stage, and cannot be hit as he catches it and for {30} frames after.
A recovery aimed at the ledge then falls past it. A special with a hitbox that arrives later hits him off it: take the ledge as the special starts.

cue.words: Fox on the ledge: it cannot be caught

lessons.title: It reacts, and it waits
text: The opponent sees what you commit to (a jump, a drop, an attack, the ledge taken) its reaction time later, and takes another way if it still has one: a Fire Fox still charging is aimed above the ledge you took.
It stalls and drifts back to come later than you expect. From high it has more ways: down onto the stage, to the ledge, or in after an attack it pulled back from.
Commit once it cannot change. CPU reaction, in the pause menu, sets how fast it sees you.

cue.words: Committed: it sees this its reaction time later

alive.words: Fox did not make it back
alive.headline: Fox was lost
alive.fix: Keep the double jump and the up special for the way back: jump toward the stage before Fox is below the ledge, or go out only as far as Fire Fox reaches.

off the ledge.expect: It does not catch the ledge
off the ledge.headline: It reached the ledge
off the ledge.fix: Take the ledge before it gets there: back to the ledge, X or Y, then an air dodge down and back on frame {J+1}.

off the stage.expect: It does not stand on the stage again
off the stage.words: it stood on the stage again, free to act
off the stage.headline: It got back
off the stage.fix: Cover where its way ends. Onto the stage: be where it lands and hit it in its landing's lag. To the ledge: take the ledge as its special starts, or hit it as it comes up from the ledge. A hit that does not take the stock sends it out again.

took the ledge.words: Fox did not take the ledge
took the ledge.headline: The ledge was free
took the ledge.fix: With Fox's back to the ledge: X or Y, then L or R with the control stick down and back on frame {J+1}, the first frame in the air. Fox slides off the edge and catches the ledge.

the stock.headline: Out of time
the stock.fix: Do not let it wait you out: go to it. A hit off the stage at its percent, or the ledge taken as it comes, takes the stock.

parts.name: Take the ledge
parts.teach: It comes back to the ledge with its jump. Take the ledge first: X or Y, then an air dodge down and back on frame {J+1}. Fox slides off the edge and hangs; it falls past. D-pad left and right: another opponent.

marks.1: Frame 1: X or Y, Fox's back to the ledge
marks.J+1: Frame {J+1}: air dodge down and back, the first frame in the air
marks.J+2: Frame {f}: Fox slides back off the edge and catches the ledge

cues.words: Air dodge down and back now

parts.name: Edgeguard
parts.teach: It will not stop until it stands on the stage: by the air, by the ledge, after every hit. It stalls, waits and takes another way when it sees what you commit to. Keep it off the stage until its stock is gone. D-pad left and right: another opponent.

marks.1: Frame 1: X or Y, Fox's back to the ledge
marks.J+1: Frame {J+1}: air dodge down and back, the first frame in the air
marks.J+2: Frame {f}: Fox slides back off the edge and catches the ledge

cues.words: Air dodge down and back now

coach.note: Taking the ledge: X or Y, then L or R with the control stick down and back on frame {J+1}. Any way that takes the stock counts.
